subject: gov.policy
name: Cost to Communicate Roadmap
milestone: Market analysis study put out to tender, reported 2026-08-01
position_start: Did not exist; no successor instrument after the 2019 Data Services Market Inquiry
position_end: Study out to tender; no roadmap published
note: the DCDT tender concedes a "current policy vacuum" and that the price benefits expected from the 2022 spectrum auction "remain largely unmet", naming market concentration, spectrum allocation and the burden on prepaid consumers as structural causes; deliverables are a Cost to Communicate Roadmap of short-, medium- and long-term reforms plus an assessment of ICASA's measures and of progress implementing the Competition Commission's 2019 Data Services Market Inquiry recommendations; the tender's issue date is not stated, so as_at is month-precision

subject: gov.policy
name: ICT indicators and scenario-modelling system to 2050
position_end: Tendered by the communications department to steer the digital economy to 2050, framed against the National Digital Transformation Roadmap, the Presidential Commission on the Fourth Industrial Revolution and the Digital Economy Masterplan; no award, value or delivery date published
note: A tender, not a system: nothing is built or awarded.

subject: gov.policy
name: Mega infrastructure project monitoring dashboard
position_end: A joint push by the Presidency and the planning and evaluation department to fast-track a digital dashboard monitoring mega infrastructure projects, put before the parliamentary committee on the Presidency alongside a wider review of progress against the state-of-the-nation commitments
note: no delivery date, data source, custodian or statement of whether the dashboard will be public is given

subject: gov.policy
name: National AI policy
milestone: Draft gazetted for comment and later withdrawn
position_end: The draft policy gazetted for comment, proposing a national artificial-intelligence commission, an ethics board, a regulatory authority and a safety institute on a phased implementation, and later withdrawn in its entirety
note: the draft was withdrawn in April 2026 after AI-hallucinated citations were found in its reference list; the redraft will issue national guidelines rather than prescribe rules to industry, the seven proposed new institutions are being reconsidered, and cabinet is targeted for November 2026 with January 2027 as fallback - South Africa has no gazetted national AI policy framework as at 2026-07-29

subject: gov.policy
name: National Policy on Data and Cloud
position_end: Gazetted as final policy, the standing national instrument on data and cloud; a policy direction of December 2025 requires data sovereignty, data protection and data security to be weighed in sector ownership regulation
sources: 2024-05-31-national-policy-on-data-and-cloud|2025-12-11-policy-direction-icasa-bbbee-data-sovereignty|2025-01-01 South African Digital Sovereignty at the Crossroad of Securitization and Development (Chapter 4) - Digital Sovereignty in the BRICS Countries
note: declares that data generated in South Africa shall be the property of South Africa and provides for in-country copies for law enforcement; Research ICT Africa warns it could obstruct the cross-border flows AfCFTA needs, and it sits markedly apart from POPIA's adequacy logic

subject: gov.policy
name: Operation Vulindlela Phase II
note: approved at the same Cabinet meeting as the Roadmap; the Q1 2026/27 report concedes progress has been uneven and in certain instances slower than initially anticipated, against the 80% on track figure of 2026-04-23 which remains the dated prior

subject: gov.legislate
name: Breach notification rate
position_end: ~244 per month (April-August 2026), on more than 8,000 security-compromise reports received to date and 1,220 since the 2026/27 financial year opened in April; the regulator projects over 3,000 for the full year and calls the rate very alarming
note: the monthly rate has eased across the three periods held while the cumulative total and the regulator's own assessment have not; the projection is the regulator's

subject: gov.legislate
name: Capital Flow Management Regulations and Crypto Asset Manual
milestone: Draft crypto asset manual for cross-border activities out for comment to 2026-09-30
position_end: Both in draft; manual comments to end-September 2026; the Treasury and the central bank published a draft crypto asset manual for cross-border activities for comment to 30 September 2026, setting authorisation and reporting rules for crypto asset service providers and defining cross-border crypto flows
note: the draft regulations were proposed by National Treasury in April 2026 and would replace the pre-approval exchange-control regime with a risk-based reporting system, carrying penalties of up to R1 million, five years imprisonment or both; the draft manual sets the rules licensed crypto asset service providers would follow on cross-border transactions and what must be reported to the Reserve Bank Financial Surveillance Department; Treasury states the manual was published before it had considered the comments already submitted on the regulations, and that both remain subject to refinement

subject: gov.legislate
name: Conduct of Financial Institutions Bill
note: would consolidate conduct rules including open finance and buy-now-pay-later

subject: gov.legislate
name: Copyright Amendment Bill
position_end: Constitutional Court ruling 2026-06
note: would replace fair dealing with a broader fair use exception; the Constitutional Court upheld most of it in June 2026 and returned parts of the education provisions as unconstitutional, so it returns to Parliament for repair; the Bill says nothing explicit about generative AI or text and data mining, which imports the American judicial answer to those questions along with the doctrine

subject: gov.legislate
name: Cybercrimes Act 19 of 2020
position_end: In force, the country's substantive cybercrime statute; the state signed the United Nations Convention against Cybercrime on 25 October 2025, and consultation on a revised National Cybersecurity Strategy is substantially complete with adoption expected in the following quarter
note: the statute is held as an excerpt; the strategy's adoption is a stated expectation and no adopted text is on file

subject: gov.legislate
name: Draft Electoral Code of Conduct on Countering Disinformation
milestone: Moving from draft to enforcement ahead of the local elections
position_end: The Electoral Commission is moving the updated code from draft to enforcement ahead of the local government elections, the existing code extended to bring it in line with campaign mechanisms on new, digital and social media and to bind political contestants, candidates and their supporters against campaigning on falsehoods, with disinformation defined as false information circulated in the knowledge that it is false. The commission cannot itself find a breach or impose a sanction: where it investigates and forms the opinion that one may have occurred it must refer the matter to the Electoral Court. Alongside the code it is working with large social-media and technology companies on self-regulation, so that false content can be referred to them for takedown
note: a draft, not promulgated regulations; the Commission's own media statement gives the comment deadline as 21 July 2026 against the 22 July on the gazetted notice

subject: gov.legislate
name: Electronic Communications Amendment Bill
position_end: Tabled by the Minister of Communications and Digital Technologies on 20 April 2026; it would empower the local-government minister to make a national standard by-law on rapid deployment of electronic communications networks. The portfolio committee extended the deadline for written submissions by one month, to 4pm on Monday 21 September 2026
note: the Bill's own text is now held, which settles the licensing exemption this row could not previously state: clause 2 amends section 6 of the principal Act to make electronic communications network services provided on a not-for-profit basis licence-exempt, and clause 3 inserts a new section 21A requiring the local-government minister to make a national standard draft by-law providing, among other things, for a uniform wayleave application and approval process

subject: gov.legislate
name: Electronic Communications and Transactions Act 25 of 2002
position_end: In force as the country's electronic transactions statute, the standing legal basis for electronic contracting and data messages
note: held as an excerpt; no amendment is on file and no repeal or successor bill appears

subject: gov.legislate
name: End-user and Subscriber Service Charter Amendment Regulations
position_end: Gazetted 2026-01-23; under review application
note: GN 7027 in GG 53991, gazetted 2026-01-23 and in force 2027-01-23: unused bundles must roll over automatically and free of charge at least once, excluding bundles of seven days or less and uncapped, free and promotional bundles, with depletion alerts at 50%, 80% and 100%; MTN and Vodacom have filed for review, and the filing date and case number are unestablished

subject: gov.legislate
name: Malabo Convention ratification position
milestone: A peer-reviewed review of four countries' health-data governance records South Africa as a non-signatory, 2026-08-14
position_end: Not held. A peer-reviewed review of health-data governance in Kenya, Nigeria, Rwanda and South Africa records only Rwanda as a Malabo Convention signatory, and finds all four frameworks fragmented, with weak cross-border transfer harmonisation and capacity gaps

subject: gov.legislate
name: Media and Digital Platforms Market Inquiry remedies
milestone: Final Report and binding remedial actions published 2025-11-13
position_end: Final Report released with binding remedial actions under section 43D(1) for Google, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI, TikTok and X; Google's Annexure 8 commitment is up to ZAR 687,500,000 over the five-year term
note: the inquiry's own Final Report and its Annexure 8 remedial actions are now held; the secondary analyst account is superseded

subject: gov.legislate
name: National Identification and Registration Bill
position_end: Still before Parliament
sources: 2026-05-29 Opinion South Africa's Digital Identity Regulations A Governance Crossroads
note: still before Parliament; named as the statutory foundation the digital-ID regulations should rest on, and the report does not say whether its passage is now a precondition

subject: gov.legislate
name: National Land Transport Amendment Act and Regulations
milestone: Act gazetted 11 June 2024; the Second Regulations gazetted 12 September 2025
position_start: Did not exist as a national registration regime reaching e-hailing services
position_end: In force: the Amendment Act of 2023 gazetted in June 2024 and the Second National Land Transport Regulations of 2025 gazetted in September 2025, which together carry the national registration regime the e-hailing licence work rests on
note: The primary instruments behind the e-hailing operating-licence regime recorded separately under Technology.

subject: gov.legislate
name: National Payment System Bill
position_end: a bill the central bank governor says will soon go out for public comment, moving payment regulation from an entity-based model to an activity-based one

subject: gov.legislate
name: OECD Common Reporting Standard regulations
position_start: The standard in force on the prior regulations
position_end: Amended regulations gazetted, updating the legal and technical basis for automatic cross-border exchange of financial-account information
note: the only cross-border data-transfer instrument on this ledger with an operating exchange behind it

subject: gov.legislate
name: Online Intermediation Platforms Guidance Note
position_end: Final guidance in force for leading online intermediation platforms, naming price-parity clauses, interoperability restrictions, self-preferencing and misuse of competitively sensitive data as the competition risks the commission will act on
note: guidance rather than regulation; no enforcement action under it is on file

subject: gov.legislate
name: Operation Vulindlela reporting
position_end: "Uneven and slower than anticipated"

subject: gov.legislate
name: POPIA enforcement notices
position_end: Four notices, May-August 2026, the fourth issued to the national bureau of standards over its 2024 ransomware attack with 90 days to revise policies, run personal-information impact assessments and implement security measures; two direct-marketing matters were also referred to the enforcement committee under POPIA section 69

subject: gov.legislate
name: Public Administration Management Act 11 of 2014
position_end: In force as the statutory frame for administration-wide arrangements across national, provincial and municipal spheres, including the transfer and secondment of employees and the establishment of common norms and standards
note: the standing statute under which administration-wide standards such as the Digital Public Services Standard are authorised

subject: gov.legislate
name: SADC real-time settlement
position_end: Kwanza added 2026-07-27

subject: gov.legislate
name: Statistics Act 6 of 1999 and Statistics Amendment Act 29 of 2024
position_start: The 1999 Act in force, the 2024 Amendment Act assented and not proclaimed
position_end: The Amendment Act proclaimed for implementation and implementation reported as progressing, with regulations and twenty memoranda of understanding under development to carry it
note: the proclamation date itself is not stated in the held account, only that proclamation had occurred

subject: gov.protect
name: Consumer Protection Act direct-marketing opt-out registry
note: 2026 CPA Amendment Regulations shift the anti-spam duty to the National Consumer Commission

subject: gov.protect
name: Operator data retention in a two-decade compensation claim
milestone: Position maintained through the Constitutional Court
position_end: The operator's position throughout a two-decade claim over a call-back product was that the data needed to value it did not exist: it told the Constitutional Court that it retains only six months of operational data at a time and that no record links a message to any corresponding or induced return call, so both sides' valuations were modelled rather than measured, off a July 2017 data-mining exercise covering six months of messages, six months of call-data records and prepaid records showing zero-airtime balances. Courts had twice ordered production, in 2011 for all product call records from 2000 and in June 2020 for data and financial information; 2016 court documents record that the operator's then financial director had proposed tracking the product
note: a retention practice tested in litigation rather than by a regulator, and the clearest published statement of what an operator does and does not keep

subject: gov.protect
name: Protection of Personal Information Act and Information Regulator
position_end: Final regulations on the processing of health information issued and effective on publication, binding on confidentiality, integrity, availability and cross-border transfer, alongside the Act's standing enforcement machinery
sources: 2026-03-06-popia-regulations-processing-health-information-2026|2026-08-17-businessday-information-regulator-sca-matric-results-popia|2026-08-18-timeslive-sahrc-personal-information-digital-age|2026-07-06-popia-five-years-nobody-accountable|2025-01-01 South African Digital Sovereignty at the Crossroad of Securitization and Development (Chapter 4) - Digital Sovereignty in the BRICS Countries
note: an adequacy model rather than hard localisation - cross-border transfers permitted where equivalent protection, consent or contractual necessity applies under s.72, with the controller accountable under s.19; the maximum fine is R10m against an IBM-measured average breach cost of R44.1m

subject: gov.standards
name: AI-in-finance regulatory framework
note: the Prudential Authority's 2025/26 report embeds AI, cloud, cyber and data-offshoring into bank supervision and ran a first nationwide AI-adoption survey, naming regulatory uncertainty, AI skills and governance as the barriers

subject: gov.standards
name: Biometric and cryptographic standards revision
position_start: Did not exist on the base
position_end: Drafts out for comment on biometric performance testing, biometric information protection and cryptographic module testing, revising the biometric interface and identification-card standards and proposing one service-management standard for withdrawal
note: the standards that would govern the biometric systems reported elsewhere in this document are being revised while those systems are already in service

subject: gov.standards
name: Crypto-asset service provider licensing
milestone: Regulator states the licensing model does not reach decentralised finance, 11 August 2026
position_end: Licensing of centralised crypto-asset service providers is in force, but the regulator states the model has no purchase on decentralised finance - protocols with no company, board or natural person to hold accountable - and plans to attach obligations elsewhere; no instrument for DeFi is published
note: 300 licences by end-2025 on the earlier source's figure; the FSCA had licensed 310 crypto asset service providers by 2026-03-31, a figure carried in the Reserve Bank's Financial Stability Review

subject: gov.standards
name: Digital Public Services Standard
position_end: In force as a national lifecycle and quality baseline for digital public services, covering accessibility, security, ethics, testing and quality assurance, deployment and retirement
note: no compliance report, assessment or departmental adoption count has been published against it

subject: gov.standards
name: ICT and Media Regulators Forum
note: Parliament's communications committee prefers strengthening ICASA, the Information Regulator, the Competition Commission and the National Consumer Commission through this forum to creating the four AI bodies the withdrawn draft policy proposed

subject: gov.discourse
name: Policy brief on information integrity and human rights
milestone: Launched at a rights commission stakeholder engagement 2026-08-19
position_end: Published by the rights commission, and launched with a deputy justice minister's statement that government should not become the custodian of truth on disinformation while the information environment should not be left to private platforms' algorithms, grounded in sections 16, 19 and 32 of the Constitution
note: a policy brief rather than an instrument; no legislative proposal or timetable follows from it on the record

subject: finance.mou
name: MzansiXchange partner institutions
position_end: Eleven institutions named as joint partners in the national data exchange pilot at its launch, the standing set of relationships underpinning it
note: no memorandum text, term or financial commitment is published for any of the eleven

subject: finance.new
name: Recapitalisation of the Vivica fibre and telecoms group
position_end: New shares subscribed across Frogfoot, Vox and Hypa at a combined after-debt equity value of R8.4bn, with the rollout to reach 360,000 connected homes a year within 12 months
note: the subscription amount is not disclosed - the R8.4bn is the implied equity value of the companies, not the money raised; the stated targets are the parties' own

subject: finance.new
name: Science and Technology Accelerator-Systems, Southern Africa
milestone: Expressions of interest opened, deadline extended to 26 August 2026
position_end: Up to GBP2.5m over three years to March 2030, of which up to GBP400,000 for 2026/27, covering artificial intelligence and emerging technologies and digital access alongside climate, energy, health and space; South Africa the primary focus, Zimbabwe and Zambia the first year's
note: at expressions-of-interest stage: the fund is resourced but the delivery consortium is not chosen, and contract signature is expected within 2026

subject: finance.new
name: Township enterprise digital and data backbone
milestone: US$1,000,000 committed to scale the platform
position_end: A United Nations development agency committed US$1,000,000 to scale a digital and data backbone for township micro, small and medium enterprises
note: a commitment record rather than a delivery report; no enterprise count, coverage or disbursement is stated

subject: infra.connect
name: 2Africa West subsea route
position_end: Open for business with South African landings at Yzerfontein and Duynefontein, an in-window addition to international bandwidth capacity
note: no capacity, price or utilisation figure is published for the landings

subject: infra.connect
name: Analogue television switch-off date
milestone: No date set; 52,869 registered households still not located
position_end: No analogue switch-off date has been set, pending a steering committee of broadcasters and stakeholders; 52,869 of the households registered for subsidised set-top boxes still cannot be located, down from about 80,000 at the previous meeting, and a data-cleaning exercise cut the installation target from 447,815 to 401,803 households against which 290,506 installations are complete and verified
note: the communications department told parliament no date has been set, sixteen years past the original 2010 deadline; estimates of households still dependent on analogue range from about 500,000 on one civil-society account to between 2.2m and 4.5m on two others, and the record reconciles none of them

subject: infra.connect
name: Cape Town internet exchange (CINX)
milestone: Two further data-centre sites live, 3 August 2026
position_end: Present at six data-centre locations after going live at two further sites, but still concentrated: one facility holds 87 of the exchange's 122 networks and nearly every 100 Gbps port, against 208 networks and 10,132 Gbps on the more distributed Johannesburg exchange
note: Distribution across sites is not the same as resilience while one facility carries most of the peering.

subject: infra.connect
name: Cell C 5G service
milestone: Went live for customers without a launch event, 2026-08-21
position_end: The third mobile operator's 5G service live for customers, claimed as the widest 5G coverage in the country because it roams on all of both larger operators' 5G sites at 2.6GHz and 3.5GHz rather than owning radio infrastructure
note: national coverage here is a contractual asset rather than a capital one; the launch carried no event and no mention in the company's maiden full-year results

subject: infra.connect
name: Data-centre incentive instrument (SEZ, depreciation, grid priority)

subject: infra.connect
name: Draft Radio Frequency Spectrum and Fees Regulations amendments
position_end: Gazetted 2026-05-15; oral hearings 19-20 August 2026
note: draft amendments to the Radio Frequency Spectrum Regulations 2015 and the Radio Frequency Spectrum Fees Regulations 2010, both published in Government Gazette No. 54677 on 2026-05-15; ICASA lists five areas - a registration regime for satellite space segment operators, revised spectrum fee formulas, blanket licensing for satellite terminal networks, protection of radio astronomy facilities and rules for Earth Stations in Motion; hybrid oral hearings at Centurion on 19 and 20 August 2026, confined to stakeholders who filed written comments

subject: infra.connect
name: Equinix Cape Town land use
position_end: Tribunal approval 2026-07-14

subject: infra.connect
name: High-demand spectrum auction
milestone: Release quantified by the 2026 National Radio Frequency Plan
position_end: The 2026 National Radio Frequency Plan targets 1,145 MHz more mid-band spectrum and over 17,250 MHz of mmWave against 794 MHz currently available - roughly 215% more high-demand spectrum cleared for release - but no auction has been scheduled, priced or gazetted

subject: infra.connect
name: IMT Roadmap 2026 and draft assignment plans
position_end: Out for consultation
note: 794 MHz assigned today against 19 625 MHz identified and 18 831 MHz to be assigned, 17 250 MHz of it mmWave with none assigned; the roadmap reaches to IMT-2030; the 850 MHz, 18 588 MHz and 215% figures in circulation are ICASA's media statement and appear nowhere in the instrument

subject: infra.connect
name: LEO satellite licensing framework
milestone: Operator pressed the regulator on licensing delay at the spectrum hearings, 2026-08-24
position_end: Direction rejected 2026-05; the minister publicly backs LEO entry while conceding licensing is the regulator's alone, and the 30% equity requirement stands
note: the operator asked how the 30% historically-disadvantaged equity requirement in the spectrum regulations applies to the new gateway and user-terminal licence categories, which the draft does not say

subject: infra.connect
name: National broadband map (DBSA)
position_end: Launched 2026-03-31
sources: 2026-03-31 SA finally has a broadband map - and it reveals where the gaps are

subject: infra.connect
name: National CSIRT (Cybersecurity Hub)
position_end: Operating; no incident statistics published
note: set up in 2015 by the then Department of Telecommunications and Postal Services under the National Cybersecurity Policy Framework; it coordinates and routes reports to a sector CSIRT or the SAPS rather than resolving them, states it has no control over investigation and resolution, and operates 08:00-16:30 on weekdays with no published out-of-hours capability; as at 2026-08-04 it published no incident statistics, advisories archive, annual or quarterly report and no data downloads

subject: infra.connect
name: National cyber-security measurement
position_end: Unchanged; no re-measurement

subject: infra.connect
name: National Cybersecurity Policy Framework
position_end: In force; the instrument the national CSIRT rests on
note: approved by Cabinet in March 2012 and named by the Cybersecurity Hub as the mandate under which it operates as the national CSIRT; established from the Hub's own site on 2026-08-04, and the framework's own text is not held

subject: infra.connect
name: National GIS infrastructure database (rapid deployment reg. 7)
sources: 2026-04-12 Icasa moves to mandate national infrastructure database
note: draft regulation 7 would compel every licensed operator to submit geo-referenced data on all passive infrastructure plus roll-out plans bi-annually to prescribed standards, with fines up to R1m

subject: infra.connect
name: National Radio Frequency Plan 2026
position_end: Gazetted 2026-07-24
note: re-bases the 8.3 kHz - 3 000 GHz allocation table on the ITU Radio Regulations 2024, keeps South Africa in ITU Region 1 with national variations only under RR 4.4, and aligns to AfriSAP and the SADC Frequency Allocation Plan; ministerial approval 2026-07-02, gazetted GN 4044 in GG 55046

subject: infra.connect
name: National wholesale 5G home-broadband network
milestone: Wholesale sales opened 2026-08; first ISP live September 2026
position_end: Selling wholesale, 5G-core only, with the first retail ISP due live in September 2026
note: a privately-financed network sold only at wholesale, with ISPs and MVNOs setting their own pricing and owning the customer relationship; the chief executive accepted the description that this is the wholesale open-access network the state spent more than a decade trying to licence and abandoned. Funded by a multibillion-rand raise after Nedbank Private Equity's December exit, with Platform Investment Partners the largest single shareholder, Wimsey Capital second, Convergence Partners and Solcon Capital continuing and RMB providing debt. No coverage footprint, site count, capacity or wholesale price is published, so what has entered service cannot be sized

subject: infra.connect
name: Radio frequency spectrum fees regulations for satellite
milestone: Draft amendment published 2026-05; operator representations filed 2026-06-29
position_end: Draft amendment under consultation, with the largest prospective entrant asking for flat per-licence fees and a ten-year minimum term
note: the representations of 2026-06-29 on the regulator's Draft Amendment of the Radio Frequency Spectrum Fees Regulations are now held first-hand, in the redacted copy the regulator published: they ask for a flat annual licence fee rather than bandwidth-based pricing, charging per licence rather than per earth-station site, blanket licensing for terminal networks including earth stations in motion, a frequency-factor table extended beyond 50 GHz, and a ten-year minimum licence duration; the submission also asks the regulator for consolidated guidance on local-entity requirements, the 30% historically-disadvantaged-group equity threshold and the ICT Sector Code, which ties the fee consultation to the ownership question the licensing framework is already stuck on

subject: infra.connect
name: SA Connect phase 2
milestone: Completion-year position in the Budget Review
position_end: Reached its 2025/26 completion year with about 1,180 km of fibre, roughly 5.6 million households reached through community wireless access and 6,343 government facilities connected

subject: infra.connect
name: Satellite market entry via section 13
position_end: Amazon Leo–Herotel, 2026-07-15

subject: infra.connect
name: Sector coverage and household internet access
position_end: Fourth-generation population coverage at 99.5% and fifth-generation at 58.0%, household internet access at 82.1% and fixed internet at home at 17.4%, with 4,377 of 21,878 government facilities connected as at October 2025
note: the regulator's own annual measurement; the 2025 edition is held as the prior and its figures are not restated here

subject: infra.connect
name: State Digital Infrastructure Company (network merger)
position_end: Implementation moved to FY2028/29
sources: 2026-04-28 State broadband merger limps into a second decade

subject: infra.connect
name: Sustainable Connectivity and Community-Led Digital Economies in South Africa Project
milestone: Launched at Inanda, north of Durban, 2026-08-25
position_end: Launched as a multi-million-rand British investment supporting local community network operators in KwaZulu-Natal's rural and township communities, already reaching parts of Ndwedwe and Inanda
note: no rand figure is published beyond 'multi-million', and no site count, subscriber target or term is stated

subject: infra.store
name: Coega artificial-intelligence data-centre campus
milestone: Direct grid connection approved by council, 27 August 2026
position_start: A proposal with no grid connection agreed
position_end: A metropolitan council approved the developer request to connect a proposed hyperscale campus at the special economic zone directly to the national utility rather than the municipal grid, for up to 556 MW, against a R3bn municipal and community infrastructure investment offered by the developer and objections from councillors
note: the connection is approved; the campus itself has no stated capacity in service, construction date or completion date

subject: infra.store
name: Development bank managed disaster-recovery service
position_end: A five-year managed service invited for information and communications technology backup, restore, disaster recovery, replication and business continuity
note: held as a procurement notice, so it establishes an intention to buy rather than a capability in service; a second development finance institution put out a server and storage upgrade proposal in March 2025

subject: infra.store
name: Domestic artificial-intelligence factory, global ranking
milestone: Entered the June 2026 global supercomputer list at rank 36
position_end: A domestically hosted artificial-intelligence factory ranked 36th on the June 2026 global list of the most powerful supercomputers: an HPE Cray XD670 of 285,696 cores on Xeon Platinum 8558 processors and NVIDIA H200 SXM5 141GB accelerators over InfiniBand NDR, installed in 2026 at a Cape Town data centre, measured at 77.79 PFlop/s Linpack against a theoretical peak of 102.16 PFlop/s
note: a capability ranking rather than a utilisation measure; no customer count, occupancy or workload figure is published, and the Linpack benchmark is a submitted result

subject: infra.store
name: Foreign hyperscaler cloud region, Johannesburg
position_start: Announced a year earlier with the city picked as the site, not operational
position_end: Operational, letting customers deploy cloud resources from a domestic location, the operator first such region on the continent
note: the operator own announcement; no capacity, customer count or investment figure is stated

subject: infra.store
name: Human rights commission inquiry into data centres
position_end: A stakeholder engagement process opened by the national human rights commission under section 184 of the Constitution and sections 13 and 18 of its own Act, to assess whether the legal, regulatory, environmental, governance and industry frameworks around data centre development meet constitutional obligations and international human rights standards. Written submissions were invited on eleven themes including electricity demand and tariffs, water use and cooling, environmental and climate impact, electronic waste, land use and community participation, data protection and privacy, transparency and accountability, business and human rights due diligence, and equitable access to digital infrastructure, closing 30 July 2026. The country's major operators - Equinix, Vantage, NTT Data, Africa Data Centres and Open Access Data Centres among them - answered publicly in August, defending their electricity and water use on their renewable-energy and resource-management programmes, one of them stating science-based climate targets and full clean and renewable energy coverage locally. The commission has published no finding, timetable or report date
note: the civil-society submission itself is not retrievable - the host serves it 403 to an automated fetch and no archive copy exists - so what is held is the announcement of it; the operators' answers are their own statements, carried in a trade account, with no independent measurement of the sector's electricity or water draw

subject: infra.store
name: Johannesburg data-centre expansion
position_end: An international operator is scaling its Johannesburg facility to 24MW and holds a ZAR7.5bn South African expansion budget covering that site plus banked land in Johannesburg and Cape Town, with further build-out held pending demand
note: the operator's own figures; no grid connection, water use or municipal approval detail is stated, and a civil-society coalition has called for deceleration and public participation in data-centre expansion

subject: infra.store
name: Open Access Data Centres acquisition of seven facilities
position_end: Seven facilities acquired from a foreign operator on 31 December 2025 after competition approval, taking the acquirer's total capacity above 25 MW
note: a domestically headquartered operator taking over a foreign one's estate; no per-site capacity or tenancy figure is published

subject: infra.store
name: Operator artificial-intelligence data-centre venture, first phase
position_end: 150MW targeted in a first phase spanning South Africa and Nigeria, in a Gulf-backed data-centre venture in which the operator group will hold only a minority stake; the vehicle is Africa Data Hub Holding and its UAE backer was named on 27 August 2026 as Tarek Al Ashram, founder of the Dubai colocation operator Gulf Data Hub, with the operator's connectivity business a shareholder supplying open-access connectivity and go-to-market support
note: no domestic site, split of the 150MW between the two countries, cost or commissioning date is stated, and the group's own half-year results booklet of 24 August 2026 had named the vehicle but not the partner behind it

subject: infra.store
name: Public participation in data-centre approvals
milestone: Objection lodged with the rights commission 2026-08-10
position_end: Not held
note: a civil-society coalition submitted concerns to the human rights commission calling for a halt on data-centre developments pending transparent public participation, citing strain on scarce water, land and electricity; no participation process, commission response or moratorium is on record

subject: infra.store
name: Rights commission inquiry into data-centre expansion
position_end: The national human rights commission is scrutinising the country's data-centre expansion, with environmental groups warning that the infrastructure required to power the state's artificial-intelligence ambitions carries costs that have not been accounted for
note: no terms of reference, hearing date or reporting deadline is published

subject: infra.store
name: Sovereign AI cloud deployment
position_end: A 7.2 EFLOPS deployment its three partners describe as Africa's most powerful AI cloud, running on more than 50 NVIDIA B300 HGX GPU servers carrying over 400 GPUs supplied through GIGABYTE's Giga Computing, in carrier-neutral Tier-3+ colocation with power supplied by the hosting partner, and pitched as keeping African AI training and inference workloads and the data behind them resident on the continent
note: the performance figure and the sovereignty framing are the partners' own announcement; no independent benchmark, customer, price or site is published

subject: infra.energy
name: Energy availability factor
position_end: The energy availability factor at 67.55%, its highest in six years, with unplanned outages down 44.5% year on year, about 1.2 million customers removed from load reduction and 505,607 smart meters installed
note: the utility's own figures; Kusile Unit 6 entered commercial operation in September 2025, adding 800 MW and completing both flagship build programmes

subject: infra.energy
name: Household electrification and the electrification grant
position_start: Household electrification at 94.7% with 1.6 million households unelectrified, on an allocation of R3.9 billion for 2025/26
position_end: Roughly R4 billion allocated for 2026/27 against third-quarter spending of 17.6% and under-expenditure of more than R190 million, attributed to late service-provider appointments and municipal non-compliance
note: about three million households are without metered supply once illegal connections are counted; the grant is being repurposed toward universal access through micro-grid and off-grid solutions

subject: infra.energy
name: Medium-term system adequacy outlook
milestone: Assessment completed on a new method
position_end: The system operator's medium-term adequacy assessment completed on a new multi-nodal, transmission-constrained method, identifying a 2029-30 adequacy risk against an unserved-energy metric below 20 GWh
note: the first transmission-constrained adequacy assessment the base holds; the risk it identifies falls inside the horizon of the data-centre load reported elsewhere on this ledger

subject: infra.capacity
name: National Integrated Cyber Infrastructure System
position_end: Operating; CHPC at maximum capacity, expansion required
note: a Department of Science, Technology and Innovation initiative implemented by the CSIR on three pillars - the Centre for High Performance Computing, which houses the Lengau supercomputer, the South African National Research Network and the Data Intensive Research Initiative of South Africa, which operates a secure national data centre; it supports the Electronic Vaccination Data System; the Portfolio Committee on Science, Technology and Innovation reported after an oversight visit that the CHPC has reached maximum capacity and that available infrastructure is insufficient for future growth

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Departmental information security officer training programme
position_end: The public service and administration department is tendering to build a training programme for departmental information security officers across the public sector, to implement the directive on public service information security
note: no officer count, curriculum, budget or compliance deadline under the directive is stated

subject: infra.cybersec
name: FSCA enforcement against online financial harm
position_end: 140 public warnings; R2.89bn penalties on 76 persons (FY2025/26)
note: the FSCA's fourth Regulatory Actions Report, for 1 April 2025 to 31 March 2026: most public warnings concerned unregistered providers promoting investment and trading offerings on social media and about 20% involved impersonation of licensed institutions, the FSCA and its own staff among them; the penalty jump is driven by the Banxso deepfake-advertising matter, over R2bn of the total, whose debarment and penalty reconsiderations were pending at the FSCA's report date

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Hungry Lion customer credential exposure
position_end: customer credentials exposed for about nine months through consumer-facing web self-service portals, on stealer-log analysis finding 23 records tied to the chain's domain, 13 of them customer accounts

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Lengau supercomputer security breach and remediation
milestone: Cause established in a written parliamentary reply, 2026-08-19
position_end: Cause attributed to vulnerabilities in the legacy high-performance computing system, with a remediation and resilience programme since run across access controls, privileged-access management, network segmentation, patch management and monitoring, and an internal accountability review still running
note: the late-May 2026 incident at the CSIR's Centre for High Performance Computing, a pillar of the National Integrated Cyber Infrastructure System, involved unauthorised access to parts of the environment and the deployment of crypto-currency mining malware; the written reply to question NW4186 states the compromise was confined to parts of the high-performance computing environment and was not a compromise of the wider system, that ageing components are no longer fully supported by their original vendors, and that the minister declines to name individuals while due process runs. No cost, data-loss finding or outage duration is stated, and the account is the department's own

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Ransomware attacker dwell time
position_end: 18 days in 2025 on a digital-forensics firm's own incident statistics, with some intrusions running start to finish inside a day, attributed to ransomware-as-a-service, automated reconnaissance and AI-assisted attacks
note: One firm's caseload, not a national series; a shorter dwell time is faster attack execution, not improved defence.

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Regional organised-crime operation
position_end: An eight-month international police operation against West African organised crime groups concluded with 58 arrests; no South African arrest, seizure or case figure is published
note: the country is not separately quantified in the account held, so the row records participation in a regional operation rather than a domestic outcome

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Subscription fraud cases against telecommunications customers and operators
position_end: 14,897 subscription fraud cases in the twelve months to April 2026, a rise of 307% on the preceding year, with every month above its counterpart a year earlier; the industry body reports social engineering over messaging, calls and text overtaking technical intrusion, and AI-generated voices and messages used to make it convincing. It describes the sector as in an active systemic-risk phase in which cyberattack, fraud, infrastructure crime, energy volatility, civil unrest, regulatory pressure, climate events and supply-chain disruption amplify one another
note: a not-for-profit industry body's own report, compiled from its member operators' case records rather than a police or regulator series; the report carries no printed publication date

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Customs-to-customs data exchange
position_end: a joint roadmap and action plan for customs-to-customs data exchange adopted by five administrations — Malawi, Mozambique, South Africa, Zambia and Zimbabwe — at a meeting in Pretoria hosted by the revenue service
note: an IT Connectivity Implementation Arrangement between SARS and the Malawi Revenue Authority for a secure electronic platform exchanging customs information in real time, aligned to the World Customs Organisation Data Model and operationalising a Customs Mutual Administrative Assistance Agreement negotiated in 2019; TradeMark Africa funded Malawi delegation attendance and continues to support implementation; no go-live date, and no purpose-limitation, retention or reciprocity terms are published

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Digital VAT model
position_end: Out to consultation: the revenue service proposes a five-corner digital VAT model of electronic invoicing, an interoperability framework and electronic reporting, moving toward VAT auto-assessment, with a phased rollout from 2026/27 and stakeholder feedback due 16 October 2026
note: a consultation paper rather than a rule; no cost to business, exemption threshold or accreditation regime for service providers is stated

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Integrated Learner Management System
position_start: Did not exist on the base
position_end: A shared post-school learner management platform piloting in sector education authorities, put at risk by an intellectual-property dispute and weak departmental buy-in reported to a portfolio committee
note: the dispute is over ownership of the platform rather than its function; no resolution, cost or pilot count is published

subject: dpi.exchange
name: MzansiXchange data exchange
milestone: Pilot infrastructure operational at the CSIR; pilot ends September 2026
position_end: Pilot infrastructure operational with Home Affairs, the social security agency, the student aid scheme and the public service department testing it, on a one-year pilot running October 2025 to September 2026 whose deliverables are four task teams, interoperability standards and draft data-exchange legislation
note: a year-long National Treasury pilot built on Estonia's X-Road; a federated real-time sharing rail rather than a central repository, nine months into pilot and onboarding additional technical capacity to support completion

subject: dpi.exchange
name: One-stop border posts and digitised border systems
position_end: Named a chairship priority for the regional bloc, tied to the corridor trip monitoring system integrating transport, immigration and customs data, to online permitting and operator accreditation, to the country's electronic visa and travel authorisation, and to a proposed regional tourism visa, with progress to be measured in border-crossing times reduced rather than agreements signed
note: the priority and the measure of progress are the chair's own; no baseline crossing time, target or timetable is published

subject: dpi.exchange
name: SAHPRA VigiFlow serious-adverse-event e-reporting pilot
position_end: Pilot open by invitation; no duration or mandatory date published
note: SAHPRA invited sponsors, applicants, clinical research organisations, investigators and holders of certificates of registration running clinical trials to report serious adverse events through the Uppsala Monitoring Centre's VigiFlow module, routing South African clinical-trial safety data through WHO-UMC-hosted infrastructure and adopting its reporting standard rather than a domestic one; no pilot duration, participant target, data-residency statement or transition date to mandatory e-reporting is published

subject: dpi.exchange
name: School administration system modernisation
position_start: The legacy system in use with no modernisation on file
position_end: User acceptance testing under way ahead of phased national implementation, with provincial education information officials and the state IT agency participating
note: the education data-coding standard of 2011 is the standing interoperability instrument behind it and has not been revised on the record

subject: dpi.id
name: Birth registration within 30 days
position_end: 680,555 babies registered within 30 days of birth in 2025/26 against a target of 677,000, with automation of the birth process in health facilities still planned for 2026/27
note: the department's own figure; no denominator of total births is given, so the share registered in time is not derivable

subject: dpi.id
name: Digital driving licence
position_end: Nearest dated milestone 2027-03
sources: 2026-01-07 Digital driving licence coming to South Africa

subject: dpi.id
name: Draft Identification Regulations amendments
milestone: Consultation closed 2026-06-06 on a 33-day comment period
position_end: Gazetted 2026-05-04 and the comment period closed on 2026-06-06. A research organisation's submission on the closing day asked the department to suspend the regulations pending a published Digital Identity Policy, an enacted National Identification and Registration Bill and demonstrated compliance with the data-protection Act, on the ground that they create a biometric enrolment, trusted-entity accreditation and real-time verification system with no formal role for the Information Regulator
sources: 2026-05-06-digital-id-draft-regulation-gazetted|2026-06-06-research-ict-africa-submission-sa-digital-id-regulations-amendment|2026-05-09-smart-ids-go-digital-draft-rules|2026-05-29 Opinion South Africa's Digital Identity Regulations A Governance Crossroads
note: voluntary digital-ID credentials with legal parity to physical ID, trusted entities granted API access to the population register under data-sharing agreements, three assurance levels, seven-year audit logs and private-sector enrolment points; finalisation dated September 2026; criticised as likely ultra vires ahead of the NIR Bill, with no right to erasure of biometric data and no citizen visibility into access logs. The submission itself is held as a supplied PDF with no published URL, so it cannot be linked to a reader

subject: dpi.id
name: Electronic travel authorisation
milestone: Launched by the president at OR Tambo 2026-08-16
position_end: Launched by the president at OR Tambo and live at four airports — OR Tambo, Cape Town, King Shaka and Lanseria — from 2026-08-12, with 6,126 fraudulent applications rejected, put at 2.8% of pilot submissions, and full visa-type rollout targeted by end-2026
sources: 2026-08-16-politicsweb-ramaphosa-electronic-travel-authorisation-launch|2026-08-13-south-africa-eta-digital-travel-four-airports|2026-08-06-wheels-up-for-electronic-travel-authorisation-visas|2026-07-28-timeslive-home-affairs-eta-digital-visa-expansion|2026-07-21-schreiber-xpatweb-global-mobility-conference-keynote|2026-06-26-sa-parliamentary-question-nw3688-source-file-eta-ttos-figures|2026-05-15-schreiber-home-affairs-budget-vote-2026-27-speech|2026-02-24 South Africa makes the ETA the cornerstone of its visa reform
note: the department publishes no statistical series and the bases do not reconcile — 88,033 applications received between 2025-10-29 and 2026-01-31 in a written reply to Parliament, over 75,000 processed with nearly 4,500 rejections at the budget vote of 2026-05-15, 203,000 processed with more than 5,700 rejected at 2026-07-21, and 6,126 rejections put at 2.8% of pilot submissions on 2026-08-13. About 85% of applications are assessed automatically against a 24-hour target and checked against 40 document-authenticity parameters, and no appeal route, accuracy rate, disparate-impact testing or human-review threshold is stated

subject: dpi.id
name: Identity documents blocked on suspicion of fraud
position_end: About 300,000 identity documents blocked, the blocks sitting behind court orders where duplicate documents or people illegally in the country were detected; the minister states that the great majority of identity-theft cases involve the manual green identity book, still held by about 16 million people
note: the minister's own figure, given in a newspaper interview; the department's answer is stated as expanding the smart identity card and the electronic travel authorisation

subject: dpi.id
name: National digital identity (credential and wallet)
milestone: Core biometric live, front end still being built
position_end: The core biometric technology live for the citizenship portal while the digital identity front end is still being built, with rollout intended during 2026 and a working single-citizen application prototype built
sources: 2026-02-17-schreiber-2026-state-of-the-nation-debate|2026-01-01-operation-vulindlela-phase-ii-progress-report-q3-2025-26|2026-05-20-home-affairs-828m-digital-id-budget|2026-03-26-dha-annual-performance-plan-2026-27|2026-04-21 South Africa's digital ID gets a targeted launch date|2026-03-30-dha-annual-performance-plan-2026-27-digital-identity|2025-03-11-digital-id-before-2029-elections|2026-01-30-digital-id-behind-schedule-mymzansi
note: core identity and PKI infrastructure hosted within the SARS environment, with SARB integrating on payments and eKYC; FY2026/27's only target is the hosting infrastructure itself, due 31 March 2027, with verifiable credentials via digital wallet in 2027/28 and digital identity and e-passports by 2029; facial recognition primary, fingerprints secondary

subject: dpi.id
name: Revised White Paper on Citizenship, Immigration and Refugee Protection
position_end: Approved by Cabinet, anchoring civil-registration reform in turning the National Population Register into an Intelligent Population Register through biometrics, interoperability and real-time integration as the foundation for digital identity, alongside digitally enabled mandatory birth and death registration
note: a white paper rather than a bill; the identification statute it anticipates is carried separately on this ledger

subject: dpi.id
name: Treasury employee verification platform
position_end: A real-time biometric employee-verification portal built for the National Treasury and linked to the population register, to detect payroll records with no matching person, with go-live stated as 15 June 2026
note: no confirmation that go-live occurred, and no count of records checked or discrepancies found, is on file

subject: dpi.pay
name: Capitec-Walletdoc merger conditions
position_end: Behavioural conditions agreed; Tribunal had not ruled at 2026-08-06
note: the Competition Commission recommended that the Tribunal approve Capitec Bank's R400 million acquisition of payment provider and system operator Walletdoc subject to behavioural conditions: the merged entity must make Capitec Pay available to third-party payment service providers technically and commercially capable of integrating with it, may not use confidential commercial information obtained through that access to compete against them, and must treat competing rails including PayShap Request and the Rapid Payments Programme no less favourably than Capitec Pay unless objectively justified by scheme rules or risk management

subject: dpi.pay
name: Cashless municipal service offices, Cape Town
milestone: Extended to three further offices from 2026-09-01
position_end: Six offices from 1 September 2026, cash no longer accepted at the counter
note: the city is extending an existing pilot at Table Bay Mall, Durbanville and Bellville motor-vehicle registration offices to customer interaction and licensing offices at Strand, Brackenfell and Kraaifontein; no figure is published for how many residents at those counters paid in cash before the change, and nothing is stated about an alternative route for the unbanked, which is the whole of the inclusion question a cashless counter raises

subject: dpi.pay
name: CIPS participation (Standard Bank)
milestone: Went live and inaugurated at the SARB 2025-11-20
position_start: No African bank held CIPS direct-participant status
position_end: Standard Bank live as the first African bank offering CIPS transactions; RMB the settlement currency
note: three separate milestones: accredited for direct-participant qualification in April 2025 (CIPS Announcement No. 108, 2025-05-12), licensed at the Lujiazui Forum in June 2025, live and inaugurated at the South African Reserve Bank on 2025-11-20 with SARB Governor Lesetja Kganyago, PBoC Governor Pan Gongsheng and CIPS chairman Wang Hongbo present; CIPS was connected to 189 countries and territories and had processed US$12.7 trillion in H1 2025 (as at September 2025)

subject: dpi.pay
name: Commercial bank technology spending
position_end: One of the large banks put total information-technology spend for the first half of 2026 at R8,779m, up 7 per cent and 28 per cent of group expenses, within non-staff costs that grew 3 per cent to R13,143m; information-technology costs at the South African bank alone rose 6 per cent to R3,800m on investment in cybersecurity, cloud and data, partly offset by infrastructure optimisation. It also took a R200m impairment on internally generated intangible assets against nil in the prior period. Digital adoption is reported by segment rather than group-wide: in personal and private banking, digitally active customers rose 10 per cent to 3.8m against total customers of 9.9m, inside a footprint of over 13.4 million customers across 17 countries
note: one bank's own results, group-wide rather than South African, so it bounds the cost of digital migration at a single institution and not the sector. The booklet does not carry the group-wide 14 per cent rise in digitally active customers reported second-hand, nor a R2.4bn 2025 software write-down; both remain the trade press's alone

subject: dpi.pay
name: Payments Ecosystem Modernisation credential and wallet
note: moved beyond conceptual design into active development of the payment credential, wallet, governance and trust capabilities, with testing against government use cases dated November 2026; the wiki holds no statement of how this state rail is meant to relate to the bank-API consolidation

subject: dpi.pay
name: Renminbi Clearing Bank of Africa
position_start: Did not exist; CIPS participation only (live 2025-11-20)
position_end: Standard Bank and ICBC jointly authorised as RMB clearing bank for Africa, with operational capacity in the 19 African countries where Standard Bank Group operates
note: the first RMB clearing bank named after a continent and the first jointly operated by two commercial banks; ICBC already acts as RMB clearing bank in 12 countries and holds a strategic equity stake in Standard Bank Group; the 19 countries are not enumerated in either the PBoC-sourced account or the bank's own as at 2026-08-04, and the designation was made by one foreign central bank with no African regulator party to it

subject: dpi.pay
name: Retail acquisition of an informal-trade payments network
position_end: an initial 51% interest acquired with effect from 14 August 2026 in a point-of-sale and vending network installed behind the counter in spaza shops and informal stores, selling prepaid airtime, electricity, gaming and entertainment
note: financial terms are undisclosed and the acquirer has not completed the initial accounting for the combination

subject: dpi.pay
name: Retail central bank digital currency
note: the SARB's published position is that a retail CBDC has no compelling case yet and that the everyday rails come first; wholesale DLT work ran through Project Khokha 1 (2018) and Khokha 2 (2022)

subject: dpi.pay
name: Scan to Pay QR scheme
milestone: Added to a handset maker's wallet, reported 31 August 2026
position_end: More than 600,000 acceptance locations and more than 19 million inclusions in consumer banking, fintech and financial service provider applications, and now available in a handset maker's wallet on eligible devices, that wallet having launched locally in November 2022
note: the acceptance and inclusion figures are the scheme provider's, carried in a handset maker's statement, with no transaction volume or value published and no relation stated to the national payment code standard

subject: dpi.pay
name: Vending and metering estate moving into electricity trading
position_end: A vending, payments and municipal-metering operator is pushing its estate up the electricity value chain on a multi-year electricity trading licence granted by the energy regulator in February 2026
note: a payments and metering estate becoming an energy trader is a use of the same rails for a different market; no traded volume, customer count or municipal agreement is published

subject: dpi.pay
name: ZARU rand-backed stablecoin
milestone: Integrated into a merchant payment infrastructure, 2026-08-19
position_end: Listed on Luno Global 2026-08-07, quoted against USDT and USDC; a merchant payments provider integrated the token into its infrastructure on 19 August, letting its commerce partners make and receive payments in it
note: issued by authorised financial services provider BlockTower and listed on Luno Global on 2026-08-07 for customers in South Africa, Nigeria, Kenya and Uganda, with Sanlam Specialised Asset Management holding the reserves and Moore Johannesburg attesting them monthly; the quoted pairs are ZARU/USDT and ZARU/USDC, so the on-chain liquidity of the rand token is denominated in dollar tokens; the account of growing merchant use is the issuer's own, with no transaction count or value published

subject: dpi.registry
name: Beneficial ownership declaration
position_start: Declaration required with no simplified channel on file
position_end: A simplified online beneficial-ownership declaration in service, with more than 23,000 declarations processed by the notice date
note: the companies commission's own figure at three weeks; no compliance rate against the register as a whole is published

subject: dpi.registry
name: Births and Deaths Registration Act 51 of 1992
position_end: In force as the statutory basis for the registration of births and deaths, the legal foundation of the civil register that feeds the population register
note: held as an excerpt; the white paper approved in April 2026 proposes digitally enabled mandatory registration under it

subject: dpi.registry
name: Blocked identity numbers
position_end: 2,202,368 identity numbers unblocked in a national review of identities blocked before November 2022

subject: dpi.registry
name: Electronic deeds registration system
position_start: The 2019 Act in force with the amended framework not commenced
position_end: Sections of the 2024 amendment in operation from 1 September 2025 and the schedule of deeds office fees replaced with a R52 lodgement fee and revised transfer-fee bands, effective one month after publication
note: the statute creating the electronic register dates from 2019 and no source states how much of the register is electronic

subject: dpi.registry
name: General Laws anti-money-laundering amendment bill
position_end: Published, requiring reporting of material beneficial-ownership discrepancies, deregistration after prolonged failure to file required registers, and tribunal review of administrative fines; not enacted
note: the enforcement half of the beneficial-ownership registers reported beside it, and it is a bill rather than a statute

subject: dpi.registry
name: Intelligent Population Register
milestone: Anchored in the approved white paper
position_end: The conversion of the population register into an intelligent population register anchored in the Cabinet-approved white paper, on biometrics, interoperability and real-time integration, with the core biometric technology live for the citizenship portal
note: cast as migration control - biometrics for every person, the green ID book to be de-recognised and the Traffic Registration Number abolished, under a Cabinet comprehensive approach for migration management; DHA has tendered a biometric case-management system and 600 handheld readers

subject: dpi.registry
name: National Population Register
note: cast as migration control - biometrics for every person, the green ID book to be de-recognised and the Traffic Registration Number abolished, under a Cabinet comprehensive approach for migration management; DHA has tendered a biometric case-management system and 600 handheld readers

subject: dpi.registry
name: Partnership beneficial owner register
milestone: Structured register and filing workflow operationalised
position_end: A structured partnership beneficial-owner register and electronic filing workflow in service, generating persistent partnership and partner reference numbers for later validation and pre-population
note: the revenue service's register runs beside the companies commission's, and no source states whether the two reconcile

subject: dpi.registry
name: SOCPEN social grant payment system
position_end: Confirmed in a ministerial reply as the system administering grant payments to more than 18 million monthly beneficiaries
note: the largest beneficiary count of any system on this ledger, and the base holds no architecture, uptime or modernisation record for it

subject: dpi.registry
name: Tax Administration Act and its 2026 amendment
position_start: The 2011 Act in force as the register's statutory basis
position_end: The amendment enacted, creating the enabling framework for a simplified customs regime for door-to-door express imports and exports and for a voluntary value-added-tax electronic reporting system
note: the electronic reporting system the amendment enables is voluntary, and no commencement or uptake figure is on file

subject: dpi.registry
name: Tax reference number enquiry service
position_end: A self-service channel on the revenue service's filing platform for retrieving and verifying a taxpayer reference number, documented in an external guide
note: a service guide rather than a service report; no usage figure is published

subject: dpi.registry
name: Uncollected identity documents
position_end: 360,000 uncollected at Home Affairs offices (2026-07-31)
note: Home Affairs opened every office nationwide from 08:00 to 17:00 on 1 and 2 August 2026 for the final voter registration weekend, stating that 360,000 identity documents sat uncollected; a valid identity document is a precondition of registering to vote, and the department published no figure for how long the documents have been waiting and no breakdown by office or province

subject: dpi.mis
name: Geospatial Information Management Strategy
position_start: Did not exist on the base
position_end: Moving toward implementation at its first provincial roadshow, with a live geospatial dashboard demonstrated and work under way with one province and one metro on spatial data governance and interoperability
note: the national spatial data instrument that the mining cadastre and the deeds register would both sit under; no adoption instrument or budget is published

subject: dpi.mis
name: Home Affairs revenue administration system
milestone: Tender revised and re-advertised, reported 31 August 2026
position_start: Advertised in June 2026 over a generic 400-plus site footprint, with standalone kiosks and the department's online channel listed as transaction channels
position_end: Re-advertised over a two-tier footprint of 275 fixed sites and 230 mobile units, with point-of-sale devices and mobile offices as the primary transaction channels and payment processing and reconciliation tied to them; the system is to handle collection, reconciliation and Basic Accounting System reporting with real-time interfaces to the service manager, live-capture, automated citizen processor and branch queuing systems, and only suppliers on the state IT agency's RFB 1183 transversal contract may bid
note: a tender, not an award: no value, closing date, bidder or delivery schedule is held, and the restriction to one transversal contract narrows the field before bidding

subject: dpi.mis
name: Land administration systems
milestone: Carried in the department's annual performance plan
position_end: Land administration and spatial systems carried as departmental commitments in the annual performance plan, against an annual report recording the state of the deeds and cadastral estate
note: both are held as excerpts and neither carries a system name, cost or delivery date

subject: dpi.mis
name: Mining Cadastre System
position_end: The provincial pilot reported complete to Parliament, a spatially defined rights register intended to improve the digital administration and transparency of mining licensing
note: no national rollout date, cost or licence-volume figure is published

subject: dpi.mis
name: National Digital Health Strategy 2019-2024
position_end: No successor strategy held
note: published by the National Department of Health with a ministerial foreword dated 2019-05-15, superseding the eHealth Strategy 2012-2016 and setting nine strategic interventions to 2024; its investment intervention proposes a national grant for digital health established with National Treasury targeting a proportionate allocation of three to five per cent of health expenditure, and it commits to a Master Patient Index for all South Africans, conformance testing of all health information systems, a health play store and a review of digital-health governance structures by 2020; the wiki holds nothing measuring what any of it delivered

subject: dpi.mis
name: NSFAS student funding system
position_end: Under administration; ICT named the largest operational risk
note: the administrator's stabilisation plan, submitted to the minister of higher education and training in the week to 2026-08-07, states that "ICT is NSFAS's biggest operational risk, as it is fragmented, manual and not fit for purpose"; the same submission reports 66 major audit findings and a disclaimer audit opinion from the Auditor-General, 115 overdue internal audit findings and nine material irregularities, five of them data or systems defects; the scheme was placed under administration in May 2026 and the governance failures referred to the Special Investigating Unit

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Batho Pele AI chatbot
position_end: DPSA-Meta-Juicetel partnership built on Meta's Llama models, providing policy, circular and legislation lookups to citizens and public servants; nine official languages targeted; explicitly decision-support only, with no decision-making authority

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Courts digitisation project
milestone: Referred to the special investigating unit and the police priority crimes unit, 2026-08-13
position_end: Records storage has been outsourced to a private contractor since 2021 across three provinces; on 13 August 2026 the justice minister referred the project to the special investigating unit and the police priority crimes unit after the contractor denied the department access to its own records at the Master of the High Court in Pretoria
note: no contract value, term, custody arrangement or data-protection provision for the outsourced court records is held, and a department locked out of its own records is a custody failure before it is a procurement one

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Digital matric certificate
note: MyMzansi's first credential use case, built with Umalusi, with pilot architecture and the verification approach in testing; the September 2026 target hardens the pilot into a production platform rather than launching it

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Digital Transformation of Government Roadmap
note: approved by Cabinet 2025-03-26 and publicly launched 2025-05-12; Cabinet's own diagnosis names interdepartmental coordination, outdated systems, overlapping mandates and limited skills - institutional fragmentation rather than technology

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Gauteng online school admissions
position_end: 2027 intake opened 2026-08-05
note: grade 1 and grade 8 applications, introduced 2016; the department reported over 1 000 applications on the opening morning; it carries a documented record of concurrency failures under load, late communication with parents, learners unplaced at the start of the academic year and manipulation by officials, and frames a better system as a future intention

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Home Affairs system downtime
milestone: 2025/26 figures given in a departmental statement and a parliamentary reply
position_end: 13,867 hours in 2025/26, a 61% reduction, with provincial gains ranging from 79% in the Free State to 41% in North West; the population register's own downtime fell from 14,720 to 11,479 hours, a 22% improvement. The department attributes it to the state IT agency moving from a bronze to a silver service level, 226 links migrated to fibre, 182 offices moved to a web service manager and 439 offices running on the identification system
note: the parliamentary reply is the fuller record and separates population-register downtime, which improved far less than the front-office figure the department led with

subject: dpi.govtech
name: IEC digital voter registration (WhatsApp and online portal)
position_end: 1.7m registration transactions over the final weekend; 291,016 first-time registrations
note: the Electoral Commission launched voter registration inside WhatsApp on 2026-08-04, three days before the registration deadline for the November local government elections, running one-time-password authentication, identity-document upload, address verification and voting-station confirmation over Meta's platform; the online portal alone carried 238,000 of the first-time registrations and 46% of all new registrations were by people under 29; no statement on data handling, and none on a fallback if the channel fails, accompanied the launch

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Inmate communication system, 243 correctional centres
position_end: A fifteen-year tender advertised for design, supply, installation, integration, operation and maintenance across 243 correctional centres, replacing copper telephony that has deteriorated beyond support
note: the Department of Correctional Services incarcerates about 166,000 people and states that the existing copper system is no longer supported; the solution is to integrate with the inmate cash system for airtime purchase, with monitoring, recording, data storage, security and compliance in scope. No contract value is published, a non-compulsory briefing was set for 2026-08-27 and bids close 2026-09-14, so nothing is awarded

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Minimum Interoperability Standards and GWEA
position_end: The sixth revision of the minimum interoperability standards framework is the standing instrument, issued by the state IT agency under the public service minister, and the successor architecture is in development

subject: dpi.govtech
name: MyMzansi single citizen application
position_end: Production-ready pilot; stable platform 2026-09
sources: 2026-08-03-itweb-mymzansi-production-ready-vulindlela-q1|2025-11-09 Behind the speedy MyMzansi screens and the Presidency's race to build a digital government|2026-02-13-sona-2026-digital-mega-platform
note: progressed from proof of concept to a production-ready pilot with governance arrangements in place; the digital matric certificate is the first credential use case; stable platform, matric credential integration and the shared Gov.za platform are targeted September 2026, with Justice, SAPS and Master's Office use cases March 2027

subject: dpi.govtech
name: National Health Insurance information architecture
milestone: NHI Phase 2 running 2026-2028, with the Act's passage before the Constitutional Court (2026-08)
position_end: In force; no implementation measurement held, with the scheme it underpins in Phase 2 and its enabling Act under constitutional challenge
note: the architecture the NHI rests on is defined inside the gazetted 2021 Health Normative Standards Framework for Interoperability in Digital Health rather than in a document of its own: a Federated Health Information Architecture hybrid of local and shared infrastructure, with central patient, provider and facility registries, shared clinical repositories and a National Health Information Exchange, built on IHE profiles, HL7 and FHIR; it supersedes the 2014 HNSF, and states that semantic interoperability remains an ongoing national undertaking with value sets to be published in implementation guides in due time. As at 2026-08 the scheme is in Phase 2, running to 2028, the Board of Healthcare Funders and the Western Cape government are challenging the Act's public-participation process in the Constitutional Court with judgment reserved since May, and the department is still building the national Health Patient Registration System

subject: dpi.govtech
name: National payment code standard (QR+)
position_end: v1.2, eight-bank test cohort

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Online Verification Service
position_end: Running since 2013 and now priced: R10 per real-time verification and R1 per batch field under section 21(2), free to state departments, municipalities and statutory bodies, in force 1 July 2025, with the revenue earmarked for the system's maintenance
sources: 2025-06-23-identification-regulations-fourteenth-amendment-gazette-52893|2025-06-23-dha-npr-verification-service-pricing-correction|2025-07-06 Home Affairs on launch of world-class new identity verification service and cost

subject: dpi.govtech
name: PayInc and the SARB stake
position_end: Bank-owned utility; non-bank shareholding ruled out (2026-07-31)
note: the Governor told the Bank's 106th ordinary general meeting on 2026-07-31 that the SARB "would have preferred to have 100% of PayInc because we want PayInc to be a payment utility. So we're not looking at bringing others in there"; Absa's chief executive put the installed base at 39 participating banks and more than 480 non-bank payment service providers

subject: dpi.govtech
name: PayShap
position_end: 905m transactions by 2026-05

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Smart ID and bank-branch channel
milestone: Minister put the channel above 450 branches as at 2026-08-24
position_end: Smart identity services running at participating bank branches - more than 450 as at 24 August 2026, against 410 live at 13 August with 574,371 applications processed through banks - and a formal departmental target of at least 200 more with a stated possibility of 750 branches during 2026/27; the department also commits to modernising 75 of the 145 remaining unmodernised local offices this financial year
note: the branch counts do not form a series - 372 and 408 one week apart in August, then 410 as at 13 August in a parliamentary reply and more than 450 stated by the minister on 24 August; the 750 figure is a possibility stated to parliament, not the departmental target

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Smart IDs issued, calendar year
position_end: Over four million smart identity documents issued in 2025/26, the highest annual output recorded
sources: 2026-05-15-dha-highest-ever-smart-id-output-2025-26|2026-01-28 Home Affairs sets new record by delivering over four million Smart IDs in 2025

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Social security agency messaging self-service channel
position_end: A messaging self-service channel letting a grant beneficiary check application status, review status and proof-of-life verification status without visiting an office, after identity verification by mobile number, one-time PIN and identity number
note: the agency frames it as paying the right grant to the right person at the right time and place, and as a way to cut queues at local offices; no usage figure is published

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Student-aid scheme systems integration
