milestone: Public Protector gave the board 30 days to produce a plan, report released 2026-08-18
position_end: The Public Protector found the scheme's systems insufficiently integrated with the home affairs, social security and revenue data sources it needs to verify students, and directed a digital modernisation and systems-integration plan within 30 days covering institutional integration, verification interfaces, fraud controls and cyber security, elimination of duplicate applications and manual workarounds, student-facing case tracking and costed milestones
note: the report draws on a 2023 investigation finding some 40,000 non-qualifying students funded to more than R5.1bn, and records that the scheme cannot resolve 80% of contact-centre queries without internal escalation

subject: dpi.govtech
name: VAT modernisation consultation paper
position_end: The revenue service released a VAT Modernisation Consultation Paper proposing a digital VAT model combining electronic invoicing, an interoperability framework and electronic reporting, aimed at moving VAT administration off manual processes and retrospective verification and into the systems businesses already run; it follows a 2023 discussion paper and is stated as building blocks rather than a decided design
note: a consultation paper: no closing date for comment, implementation timetable, cost, mandate threshold or legislative vehicle is stated in the account held

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Western Cape funding-matching platform for small business
position_end: Free access for micro, small and medium enterprises in the province to a matching platform covering over 300 funders and 600 finance products
note: the platform is a private one and the funder and product counts are its own; the same data put 65.3% of provincial applicants as unable to supply their latest financial statements

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Western Cape Infrastructure Virtual Platform (EVE AI agent)
milestone: Launched at inaugural Infrastructure Ministerial Roundtable, 2026-07-30
position_end: Automatically evaluates projects against Treasury rules and ISO 9001 via AI agent EVE; evaluated pipeline of 52 projects worth R132bn, 11 worth over R20bn to be released to market; MoUs signed with Infrastructure South Africa, IFISA, EDC South Africa and UCT

subject: digital.localgov
name: Emfuleni electronic records management system
milestone: Award recorded in quarterly procurement reporting
position_end: An in-house server-based electronic records-management system awarded on a three-year term from October 2025, recorded in the municipality's quarterly procurement report
note: known only through a procurement annexure, so the award is established and the deployment is not

subject: digital.localgov
name: Home Affairs offices inside municipal buildings
position_end: An appointment-only office opened inside the Cape Town Civic Centre on 24 August 2026, which the city describes as the first municipal facility to host a national home affairs office; 148 people applied for services on the opening day, and the office is positioned to relieve the department's central business district office. Atlantis is named as the next priority in the city
note: the minister frames it as part of a strategy to decentralise access across bank branches, malls, smartphones and municipal buildings rather than concentrate it in departmental offices

subject: digital.localgov
name: Mangaung metro records digitisation
milestone: Programme status reported to the NCOP
position_end: An information and communications technology roadmap, a document-management rollout and digitisation of hard-copy and historical municipal records reported to the National Council of Provinces, with budget, legacy-system and skills constraints named
note: the metro names its own constraints, which is rarer on this ledger than the programme itself

subject: digital.localgov
name: Municipal revenue management plan
position_end: The local government association has issued a request for proposal for consultants to build a plan covering credible billing systems, collection strategies, recovery of long-outstanding debt and indigent management across the 257 municipalities it represents. The request puts municipal consumer debt at about R467.2bn and municipalities' own debt to creditors at about R160.8bn, states that many municipalities collect less than 70 per cent of billed revenue, and attributes about R25bn of annual water and electricity revenue loss to leaks, theft, illegal connections, inaccurate or outdated meters and weaknesses in metering and billing systems
note: unverified indigent registers and data deficiencies are named among the losses the consultants are to identify and quantify; no award, budget or timetable is stated

subject: digital.localgov
name: National archives guidance on managing electronic records
position_end: Standing guidance from the national archives on managing electronic records, the rule set the municipal digitisation programmes on this ledger are obliged to work to
note: an undated guidance page; no compliance assessment against it appears for any municipality

subject: digital.rural
name: Deeds registry service continuity after fire
milestone: Service moved to a new location
position_start: Did not exist as a recorded event
position_end: All paper records of registered land at one regional deeds registry already back-scanned into the electronic deeds system when the building burned, carrying service continuity to a new location
note: the clearest evidence on this ledger that back-scanning of a regional registry had actually been completed, and it is evidenced by a fire

subject: digital.rural
name: Electronic medical record implementation in eight provinces
position_end: Public-health service providers invited to implement the electronic medical record solution across eight provinces, with a provincial deployment already recognised in the Free State where training, connectivity, cybersecurity and interoperability are recorded as outstanding
note: the bid is held as an excerpt and no award, value or facility count is on file

subject: digital.rural
name: Integrated person management at police stations
milestone: Site count given to Parliament at 31 March 2026
position_start: Did not exist on the base
position_end: The count of police sites with integrated person management implemented given to Parliament as at 31 March 2026, with personnel, connectivity, rugged devices and scanners named as the dependencies for wider rollout, alongside station hardware and network rollout counts and an electronic policing policy directing digital docket management into pilot stations
note: the dependencies named are physical rather than software, which is what makes rural rollout the binding case

subject: digital.rural
name: KwaZulu-Natal Digital Access Programme
milestone: Launched at a rural primary school
position_end: A provincial treasury programme for rural and under-resourced schools launched in one district, with announced expansion to two further districts
note: no school count, budget or device figure is published; the national digital education strategy of September 2025 is the policy frame it sits under

subject: digital.rural
name: Off-grid school media lab
position_end: A containerised off-grid media lab in service at one primary school, with solar generation and battery storage, offering coding and robotics training to surrounding schools
note: one site; the off-grid design is the notable part, against the rural electrification position reported on this ledger

subject: tech.ai
name: Appeal on algorithmic eligibility verification for the SRD grant
milestone: Argued before the Supreme Court of Appeal 2026-08-25
position_end: the state's appeal against the January 2025 high court ruling on the online-only relief grant argued in Bloemfontein on 25 August 2026, with judgment reserved pending further affidavits
note: this is the closest thing the record holds to a rule on state automated decision-making, and it is litigation rather than an instrument; no judgment in the appeal is on file and the row governing rules for state automated decision-making remains Not held

subject: tech.ai
name: Automated selection at SARS
position_end: 100% of verifications, 88.41% of complex audits

subject: tech.ai
name: Centre for Artificial Intelligence Research
position_end: A distributed national research network in artificial intelligence hosted across universities with a national coordinating centre, the country's standing public research capability in the field
note: an undated institutional page carrying no funding, headcount or output figure; the comparative study of national strategies places the country's policy position rather than its research base

subject: tech.ai
name: Customer-facing AI assistant at a major bank
position_end: An agentic artificial-intelligence chatbot handling over 100,000 queries a month from about 1.6 million users in the first half of 2026, alongside 30,000 employees a month on a vendor productivity assistant, more than 3,800 staff-built automation agents in production and over 1,400 developers on AI-assisted coding tools
note: the bank's own figures, reported at interim results; a different institution from the enterprise-adoption row above and not comparable with it

subject: tech.ai
name: Enterprise AI adoption at a major bank
position_end: More than 39,000 staff, 72% of the workforce, reported as active generative-artificial-intelligence users on a multi-model enterprise platform hosted on a foreign cloud provider, with relationship management, servicing, payments and lending named as the four priority areas
note: the bank's own figures for active users, not for automated decisions or customer-facing deployment; no model inventory, assurance process or customer disclosure is stated, and the country holds no artificial-intelligence incident or assurance register

subject: tech.ai
name: Institutional policy on artificial intelligence in higher education
milestone: Absence set out in university research presented 2026-08-17
position_end: Not held
note: research from a South African university finds artificial-intelligence adoption in teaching and assessment outpacing institutional policy, with lecturers reporting inconsistent or absent guidance on accountability, the reliability of detection tools and academic integrity; no sector-wide instrument or regulator guidance is held

subject: tech.ai
name: Machine-learning screening of travellers for fraud
position_end: Stated intention to screen travellers for fraud using machine learning; no system, procurement, legal basis, accuracy measure or appeal route is published
note: An intention reported in the trade press; no instrument establishes it.

position_end: Issued 2025-09-26; product registration not commenced

note: the account is the insurer's own; no model, accuracy measure, decision it feeds or governance arrangement is stated

subject: tech.ai
name: Western Cape AI Cluster and its responsible-AI programme
milestone: Programme announced 17 August 2026, first summit 25 August 2026
position_end: A responsible-AI programme announced on 17 August 2026 under a newly created provincial AI cluster, run with the provincial economic development department, whose first summit at Cape Town on 25 August 2026 covered AI policy, governance, infrastructure investment and sovereign AI; it was convened after the national department withdrew the draft national AI policy
note: a provincial and industry-association initiative, with no budget or work programme stated

subject: tech.industry
name: B-BBEE ICT Sector Council
status: Implemented, chair replaced on an interim basis
milestone: Interim chair appointed for six months, reported 2026-08-14
position_end: The communications minister replaced the council’s chairperson and appointed an interim chair for six months after a departmental investigation found the council dysfunctional; the investigation report is not published, and no remedial plan, terms of reference for the interim period or date for a permanent appointment is stated

subject: tech.industry
name: Cell C financial turnaround
milestone: R4.9bn write-down of the stake by its listed holder
position_end: Its listed holder booked a R4.9 billion full-year loss writing the stake down to the operator's R9 billion listing price and now holds 49.53% of it, with net income 297% down year on year on the write-down alone
note: an asset-light model on other operators' radio networks, so the wholesale growth is a virtual-operator business rather than network build

subject: tech.industry
name: E-hailing operating licence regime
milestone: Western Cape undertook to add e-hailing to its licence application, 21 August 2026
position_start: A national registration regime under the National Land Transport Amendment Act, 2023 and the Second National Land Transport Regulations, 2025, with provincial application forms not yet carrying e-hailing as a service option
position_end: A platform carried its compliance programme into the provinces — a North West regulatory engagement in Rustenburg on 18 August 2026 attended by more than 150 operators, and a Western Cape transport dialogue in Cape Town on 21 August at which the provincial mobility department's director of licensing and adjudication undertook to add e-hailing as a service option on the operating-licence application; the North West provincial regulatory entity put its pending operating-licence backlog at 3,000 to 5,000 applications
note: the account is the platform's own and the undertaking is not yet an amended form; the platform states it was among the first to receive a Certificate of Registration from the national regulator, in February 2026

subject: tech.industry
name: Informal-retail transaction data product
milestone: Rebranded into a consolidated merchant division 2026-08-19
position_end: A listed payments company sells near-real-time item-level intelligence on the informal retail economy, drawn from a point-of-sale network of over 90,000 spaza shops and taverns and 10,500 checkouts, to consumer-goods brands, wholesalers and financiers
note: the network figures are the company's own; no consent basis, pricing or data-protection assessment for the resale of merchant transaction data is stated

subject: tech.industry
name: Mobile virtual network operator subscriptions
milestone: Operator results for the 12 months to 2026-05-31, presented 2026-08-21
position_end: About 4.4 million active MVNO SIMs at end-2025 on an analyst count, up about 43% year on year and forecast to reach 14.4 million by 2030; the fourth-largest of the five mobile operators reported 5.7 million MVNO subscribers carried on its own wholesale platform for the 12 months to 2026-05-31, which it put at an estimated 80-85% share of the market
note: two different bases, not a series: the 4.4 million is an analyst house's count of active SIMs at end-2025 with no published methodology, and the 5.7 million is one operator's own count of subscribers on its wholesale platform to 2026-05-31. The analyst report puts South Africa first on the continent and forecasts that South Africa, Nigeria, Kenya and Uganda together will hold 85% of Africa's 39.6 million MVNO subscribers by 2030

subject: tech.industry
name: Platform programme for news creators
position_end: Eight South African news creators joined a technology company's growth programme for independent news publishers
note: a company programme with eight named places, running against the same company's market-inquiry findings and remedy that this base records separately

subject: tech.innovate

milestone: Opened at The Innovation Hub, Pretoria
position_end: Opened with the International Telecommunication Union as part of its network of acceleration centres, to support information and communications technology small enterprises and digital entrepreneurs across the continent
note: no tenancy, cohort or funding figure is published

subject: tech.innovate
name: Domestic scale-up fund
position_end: A domestic small-enterprise investment firm launched a R350m fund to back high-growth African scale-ups
note: a launch rather than a deployment; no first investment, sector focus or ticket size is published

subject: tech.innovate
name: Mamor Capital Ventures first fund
position_end: First close at R300 million (US$18.8 million) against a R550 million (US$34.4 million) target, anchored by the state asset manager, to invest in post-revenue South African technology companies
note: a first close is committed capital rather than deployed capital; no deal count, cheque size or sector split is published, and the firm states it spent more than three years raising it

subject: tech.innovate
name: Small business incubation and digital hubs
position_end: The small business department's standing network of incubation and digital hubs, the state's own hub estate beneath the two centres opened in the window
note: an undated programme page with no hub count, spend or enterprise figure

subject: tech.innovate
name: South African Centre for Industry and Technology
position_end: Launched hosted by a university in partnership with an international forum, opened alongside a G20 research and innovation working group ministerial
note: no programme, budget or occupancy is published; it is the second hub opened in the window

subject: capacity.literacy
name: Household and individual internet use survey
position_end: The one nationally representative demand-side survey of internet access and use the base holds, covering household and individual access, use and affordability
note: held as an excerpt and two years old at the window's close; no digital-literacy or digital-skills rate is measured in it or anywhere else on this ledger

subject: capacity.literacy
name: Western Cape eCentre network
position_start: The network operating with no count on the base
position_end: The 83rd brick-and-mortar eCentre opened, adding a business corner, public access centre and training centre to a network also served by a mobile eCentre
note: a provincial network; no user, training or throughput figure is published for it

subject: capacity.training
name: Data-centre operations academy
milestone: Two domestic firms joined and funded a full 2026 cohort
position_start: An academy without industry-funded places at cohort scale
position_end: Two domestic firms joined as industry partners and are sponsoring a full candidate cohort for the 2026 intake, the first South African firms to fund a whole cohort, one opening a newly launched Midrand OEM training facility and the other a live operational data centre to supply the practical component of a graduate-to-employment pipeline its founder frames as a recruitment expense rather than a training one
note: no cohort size, placement rate or cost per place is published

subject: capacity.training
name: Digital Skills Impact Fund
position_start: A R200m fund open through fixed application windows
position_end: The R200m fund moved to year-round applications for co-funded work-integrated digital skills programmes, which have taken more than 1,800 young people across all nine provinces, 97% of them absorbed into employment and over 75% still employed after six months, against the operator's targets of 40,000 digitally skilled workers a year by 2030 and 500,000 young people into digital roles by 2034

subject: capacity.training
name: Digital-skills pipeline from school to employment
milestone: Reviewed in a report with the higher education department, 2026-08-14
position_end: Constrained at both ends and structurally so: employers report about 7 per cent of ICT and engineering posts unfilled, with software developers (380), network engineers (285) and ICT security specialists (130) the hardest-to-fill roles, while 44.8 per cent of online vacancy postings ask for transversal digital skills, 30.9 per cent for basic ICT skills and 26.4 per cent for advanced ones; employers attribute the gap 26 per cent to shortfalls in basic-level training, 24 per cent to graduate pipeline throughput and 21 per cent to the pace of technological change (2026-06)
note: a development bank's report, philanthropically funded and produced with the higher education department; the feature carries the finding rather than the underlying figures

subject: capacity.training
name: Industry Connect ICT jobs portal
milestone: Portal launched by the ICT industry association, 2026-08-28
position_end: A portal launched by the ICT industry association to link employers, ICT jobseekers and graduates and professional development in one platform rather than as a conventional job board, its stated purpose being the disconnect between people holding ICT skills and the businesses that need them; it arrives as government and business enter the third phase of a partnership to create a million jobs by 2030. No listing count, placement figure, funding or operator arrangement is published
note: an association's own launch announcement carried in a trade account; nothing establishes whether any employer or jobseeker is yet on it

subject: capacity.training
name: National Digital and Future Skills Strategy 2020
position_end: Under review; no replacement
note: the 2020 strategy is under comprehensive review, disclosed in a written parliamentary reply rather than announced; DCDT declined to forecast AI's net employment effect, holding that it depends on the country's ability to equip workers

subject: capacity.training
name: Vendor digital-skills programme in Northern Cape schools
milestone: Partnership announced 2026-08-18 for classes from February 2027
position_end: A networking vendor's academy and a private group agreed with the provincial education department to take networking, cyber security and artificial-intelligence courses into 235 schools, as extracurricular classes for grades 10 to 12 beginning February 2027, inside a global skills-to-jobs programme the vendor states has trained more than 600,000 South Africans
note: announced for a start five months away; no learner target, cost, funding split, teacher-training provision or certification pathway is published, and the 600,000 figure is the vendor's own

subject: capacity.research
name: Standing in digital-privacy research
position_end: 18th worldwide and the only African country in the top 20 for digital-privacy research output, on a 4,760-article review of 2005-2025
note: a bibliometric analysis of 4,760 Scopus and Web of Science articles over twenty years, published in a South African journal; the same review finds refugees, people with disabilities, older people and racial and ethnic minorities notably underrepresented in the literature, so the ranking measures volume of output and not coverage of the populations most exposed

subject: include.access
name: Bank self-service kiosk network
position_end: 581 self-service kiosks handling more than half a million transactions a month across over 60 banking services, through which almost 70% of instant-issued debit cards are dispensed and 56% of kiosk-issued cards go to entry-level clients; mall-based zones pairing kiosks with consultant support enter pilot at a Johannesburg mall in late August 2026, with wider deployment flagged for the mid- to long term
note: one bank's own figures; no regulator series covers self-service banking channels

subject: include.access
name: Bank-account means test across eight grants
position_end: Undecided; SCA hearing 2026-08-25

subject: include.access
name: DCDT expenditure
position_end: R3.61bn of R3.74bn spent, FY2025/26

subject: include.access
name: Disability-inclusive data cooperation with China
position_end: A seven-point plan agreed to deepen cooperation on disability-inclusive data, universal design and artificial-intelligence-enabled assistive technology, anchored in a proposed disability centre of excellence working with the national statistics office
note: no instrument, funding, timetable or data-sharing arrangement is published for cooperation that names a national statistics office as a partner

subject: include.access
name: Employment Services Amendment Bill
position_end: Published, extending the statutory employment-services framework to foreign nationals, refugees and asylum seekers, creating work-authorisation verification and requiring a framework for collecting information on their recruitment and employment
note: the verification duty it creates would run against the population register; the 1998 refugees statute is the standing frame it amends around

subject: include.access
name: MICT SETA
position_end: Referred for assessment 2026-07-21

position_end: a national financial-education week run from 24 to 30 August 2026 by the committee the Treasury and the conduct authority established to co-ordinate financial literacy

subject: include.access
name: Municipal citizen service application
position_end: A digital service-reporting channel letting residents log and track requests and receive municipal updates
note: one small municipality; no user or request figure is published

subject: include.access
name: National study on digital gender transformation
position_end: A national study announced by the gender equality commission on women's participation in the digital economy, aimed at producing gender-responsive policy recommendations to close the digital access gap
note: the standing instrument beside it is a gender-responsive planning and budgeting framework, which is a budgeting method rather than a digital measure

subject: include.access
name: Postbank Black Card migration
position_end: 172,146 replaced by 2026-07-28; 264,263 outstanding
note: of 463,836 active gold cards at 2026-04-29, 172,146 had been replaced by 2026-07-28, 8,119 subsequently dropped off the SASSA file and 264,263 remain, roughly 40% of them in KwaZulu-Natal and Gauteng and 43,515 in the Western Cape; Postbank reports 306 replacement sites against a target of 300 plus nine mobile teams, ring-fences customers more than 30km from a site, and plans the rollout from monthly SASSA data on the location of each customer's last three transactions

subject: include.access
name: Roads4U road-defect reporting application
position_end: A public road-defect reporting application that geolocates each report and routes it to the responsible road authority, issuing reference numbers and status updates to the reporter
note: the routing and the reference number are what distinguish it from a complaints inbox; no volume figure is published

subject: include.access
name: SASSA biometric verification against Home Affairs

subject: include.access
name: SASSA grant reviews
milestone: Nationwide review audit reported at 105,600 of 352,000 targeted reviews completed
movement: Advanced in scope, regressed in access
position_end: 105,600 of 352,000 targeted reviews completed and an estimated R450 million saved, with lawful beneficiaries’ payments suspended without effective notice
note: The savings figure is the agency’s own estimate; the suspensions are reported against it.

subject: include.access
name: SITA performance
milestone: Public Service Commission probe reported to Parliament, August 2026
